title: Prepare our planned dish safely
outcome: FOODWISE: prepare a 2-3 step dish safely.
goal: I can follow my checked plan to prepare a simple dish and show safe working.
success: I can complete the agreed preparation steps with the support I need.
I can show hygiene and safe tool use before, during and after making.
I can keep an honest record of my finished plate and the support used.
dish: Cold bean and vegetable wrap with fruit and plain yoghurt
portion_note: These are the Week 1 model quantities for one person. Use the pupil’s actual approved plan and any checked substitution. Individual needs and appetite vary. One 60 g yoghurt portion is split: about 20 g in the filling and 40 g alongside.
steps: After the adult’s checks, wash hands with soap and water and dry them. Wash the carrot, cabbage and apple. Grate the carrot and finely slice the cabbage with adult-approved tools and supervision. Use prepared vegetables if agreed.
Mash 80 g of cooked beans labelled ready to eat with a fork. Mix in about 20 g from the single 60 g yoghurt portion. Add the carrot and cabbage. An adult opens tins and removes sharp lids.
Put the filling on the wholemeal wrap and fold it. Serve with the apple and the remaining yoghurt. Ask the adult to check the plate and store or serve it safely. Tasting is optional.

Before: Adult clears the private allergy and dietary checks from current school records and actual ingredient labels.
Wash and dry hands. Clean the surface and tools. Tie hair back and cover cuts.
Use the checked plan, agreed tools and cooked ready-to-eat beans. Keep chilled food refrigerated until needed.
During: Use only approved tools with the agreed supervision. Put a tool down before asking for help.
Keep food and utensils protected from raw-food contamination and allergen cross-contact. Use clean utensils and do not share tasting spoons.
If there is a spill, a cut, an unexpected ingredient or uncertainty, stop and tell the adult. Keep chilled food out for the shortest preparation time.
After: Adult agrees immediate serving, refrigeration at 0–5°C, or disposal. Follow use-by and storage instructions.
Adult transfers unused beans from an opened tin into a clean covered food container before refrigeration.
Clear and clean using the agreed routine. Put waste away, wash hands and complete the actual record.

adult_gate: Before ingredients are issued, use the school allergy policy and individual healthcare/access records, complete the blank teacher note privately, check every actual label and substitution, and confirm trained supervision, emergency arrangements, handwashing, safe tools, clean preparation and chilled storage. Unknown or incomplete checks mean HOLD. Do not infer no allergies from a blank record.
storage: Keep chilled food at 0–5°C and out for the shortest practical time. Follow the earliest relevant use-by and storage instructions. Plan same-day eating. Agree safe chilled transport before food is taken home. Refrigerate leftovers promptly; use within 48 hours or freeze if suitable, following labels. An adult decides storage or disposal. Never refrigerate beans in their opened tin.
no_kitchen: Use the same planned cold wrap with adult-supplied washed, pre-cut vegetables and cooked ready-to-eat beans. Pupils mash, mix, fill and fold using a fork, bowl and clean work surface. No heat or knife is needed. Staff must still approve handwashing with potable water, cleaning, food-safe preparation, labels, allergy controls, supervision and verified cold storage. A checked insulated cold container may be used only if it holds food at 0–5°C. If any requirement cannot be met, use the materials-free simulation and keep practical competence pending.
fallback: With no safe food facilities, food or equipment, rehearse with empty hands or pictures. The pupil explains or directs the three steps and names a safety action at each point. Record this as planning or simulation, not preparation. Mark the practical and any plate photo pending. Rebook the practical when the adult can meet all safety requirements.
photo: An adult may use an approved device after food handling has stopped. Photograph only the pupil’s actual food on a plain surface. Keep all people, faces, hands, names, labels, screens and reflections out of the frame. No automatic upload or public posting. Verify a copy with location and other identifying metadata removed before attaching it to private evidence. Keep the device away from food preparation. Restore hand hygiene if returning to food. If a suitable device or checks are unavailable, leave photo status pending and use a truthful written or drawn plate record. Never use the generated recipe pictures as pupil evidence.

Supported: Use one picture and instruction at a time with an adult.
Direct or complete the agreed action. Ask for prepared vegetables or adult tool handling if needed.
Name one hygiene action and keep your own actual plate record.
Record exactly which actions you did and which the adult did.
Standard: Follow your checked three-step plan and use the agreed tool routine.
Check hygiene before, during and after making. Stop if anything changes.
Complete your plate and explain one safe action you took.
Record an actual change, support and the adult’s storage decision.
Stretch: Complete the core practical and evidence first.
Explain how one choice controlled a food-safety risk.
Compare your finished dish with the Week 1 plan and justify a real change.
Suggest one improvement for the next preparation without claiming a taste you did not try.

vocabulary: Get food ready using the agreed method.
Actions that keep food and equipment clean and safe.
Food that needs no further cooking before eating.
An allergen gets into another food through contact.
Keep food cold at the agreed safe temperature.
A truthful record of what actually happened.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Show one picture and step at a time. Model the first action, then fade. Keep quantities visible. Check understanding before any tool use. Offer a spoken sequence and repeated hygiene prompts.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Accept pointing, speech, signing or pupil-directed adult handling. Ask one short question and allow thinking time. Read the evidence words back for confirmation.
adaptations.SEMH: Offer a calm pause with tools down and food protected. Agree a return cue. No public performance, compulsory tasting, home-finance talk or personal health disclosure. Use a private adult check.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Offer prepared vegetables, an approved adapted tool or pupil-directed adult handling. No touching or tasting is compulsory. Record the actual role rather than claiming an unperformed skill.
adaptations.EAL: Plan and rehearse in any language. Pair the picture with the spoken action and quantity. Confirm meaning before tools are issued. Read the pupil’s recorded explanation back.

careers: Food preparation teams use clear methods, safe tools and accurate records. They adapt a plan while keeping the person eating the food safe.

stages.name: Arrival
stages.title: Our checked plan
pupil: Find your Week 1 plan and agreed method.
Wait for the adult’s GO before food is issued.
Wash and dry your hands.
stages.teacher: Complete the private records, label and facilities checks before the lesson and keep the allergy note blank in the public master. Read each pupil’s plan and confirm any substitution. Give GO only for a cleared practical; unknown checks mean HOLD. Pupils wash and dry hands. Use the cold assembly fallback if safe facilities are approved, otherwise simulate. No one must disclose personal health information to the group.
stages.check: Ask: What must happen before ingredients are issued? Expect the adult’s completed safety and allergy checks, then GO. An unchecked or blank note is HOLD, not clearance.

stages.name: Starter
stages.title: The three steps
pupil: Put prepare, mix and assemble in order.
Match the pictures to your own checked plan.
Name the cooked beans we may use.
stages.teacher: Use the original model picture strip and the step card. State that the illustrations are teaching models, not photographs of pupil work or proof of quantities. The written plan controls actual amounts. Use only cooked beans labelled ready to eat. Never use dry or merely soaked beans in this cold dish.
stages.check: Correct order is prepare, mix, assemble. If a pupil cannot explain the order, use one picture at a time and repeat the first step together.

stages.name: I do
stages.title: A safe demonstration
pupil: Watch the adult show the agreed tool routine.
See how one yoghurt portion is split.
Ask for a prepared ingredient or a different approved tool if needed.
stages.teacher: On a clean station demonstrate the locally approved grater or knife method, keeping fingers away from cutting surfaces and the board stable. Adult opens tins and removes sharp lids in advance. Show a fork mash and about 20 g from the single 60 g yoghurt portion. Keep the rest chilled for the side. Model clean utensils, stop-and-ask, and the no-tool route. Do not require tasting.
stages.check: Ask: Which beans, and who opens a tin? Expect cooked ready-to-eat beans and the adult. If not secure, use prepared ingredients and recheck before pupil tool use.

stages.name: We do
stages.title: Prepare together
pupil: Use step 1 with the agreed support.
Wash produce and prepare the vegetables.
Keep your station and utensils clean.
stages.teacher: Supervise the pupil’s approved tool action closely or provide washed prepared vegetables. The pupil may direct adult handling. Issue only needed portions and keep other chilled ingredients in storage. Prompt one action, wait, then fade support. Place used equipment in the agreed cleaning area as tasks finish. Check the private plan if a food changes.
stages.check: Look for actual handwashing, clean surface, safe approved tool use or pupil-directed adult handling. Record what the pupil did and the adult did. Do not infer a cutting skill from an assembled wrap.

stages.name: We do 2
stages.title: Stop and check
pupil: A new yoghurt appears that has not been checked.
Choose: use it, ask a friend, or stop for the adult’s label check.
Start mixing only after the check is clear.
stages.teacher: Run the short hinge within the practical. Correct answer is stop for the adult’s label check against the individual plan. A familiar-looking pot or plant alternative is not clearance. If any pupil misses this, stop their food handling and reteach before restart. Parallel check: a utensil touches an unapproved food; stop, isolate it and get a clean approved utensil after the adult check. Pupils then begin the fork mash with the agreed ingredients.
stages.check: All pupils show or say stop-and-check before continuing. The adult resolves the actual concern; a quiz answer alone does not clear an ingredient.

stages.name: Independent
stages.title: My planned dish
pupil: Mash and mix the filling with the agreed amounts.
Fill and fold the wrap. Serve the sides.
Keep tools safe and stop if anything changes.
stages.teacher: Pupils complete steps 2 and 3 under ongoing supervision. Independent is the timetable stage, not unsupervised tool use. Keep the Week 1 plan beside the station. Accept support and pupil-directed adult handling, recorded honestly. Check one 60 g yoghurt allocation, actual portion choices and any approved substitution. Support should fade only when safe. Pause with tools down and food protected whenever needed.
stages.check: Look for the actual agreed dish, clean handling and safe responses. If incomplete at the stop point, store or dispose safely and record the true stage. Do not rush sharp tool work to finish.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: The plate and clean station
pupil: Put tools down and ask for the plate check.
The adult may take a food-only photo.
Follow the storage and cleaning routine.
stages.teacher: Check the dish and the storage or serving decision first. Stop food handling before an adult operates the approved device. Frame food only and keep capture optional. The adult must verify the private evidence copy has no identifying content or metadata; otherwise leave photo pending. Return utensils, clean surfaces, put waste away and wash hands. Start clearing progressively earlier if the group needs longer.
stages.check: A photo shows the plate, not safe preparation. Combine it with brief adult observations of actual hygiene, tool use and support. Tasting is optional and any uneaten food follows the adult’s safe decision.

stages.name: Exit
stages.title: My honest record
pupil: I prepared ___ with ___ support.
One safe action I used was ___.
My plate photo is stored privately / pending.
stages.teacher: Use the evidence sheet and photo record. Retain actual dish, any change, support, observed safe actions, plate photo location or pending status, and the storage decision. A written or drawn plate record can supplement a missing photo, but never label it as a photo. Keep Week 3 evaluation for the next return. Completed private allergy notes and photographs stay out of published teaching files.
stages.check: Keep preparation, adult handling, simulation and photo status separate. Let the pupil correct the record. Record an unfinished or unsafe attempt honestly and plan a supported next opportunity.

misconceptions: A familiar ingredient is automatically safe.
Every actual label and substitution must be checked against current individual records before use.
A cold dish needs no food safety checks.
Handwashing, clean preparation, approved ingredients and chilling still apply.
A plate photo proves safe preparation.
It shows the food. Adult observations record the actual process and support.
A simulation is the same as a practical.
Label rehearsal as simulation and keep preparation competence pending.
